subject: Pilot purchase: invoice path options + co-sell revenue share questions
messages:
From: Emily Santos <emily.santos@medipath.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@medipath.com>, procurement@medipath.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot procurement questions — marketplace vs direct invoice

Neha / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency and the runtime controls. We are ready to scope a 3-month pilot focused on internal clinical summarization (PII redaction, short-context summaries). Before we proceed to an NDA and PO, procurement asked me to clarify a few things: 

- If we purchase via AWS Marketplace (private offer), what is the expected invoice cadence and who is the Seller of Record?
- If we do a direct purchase (Redwood invoice), can we get co-sell credits or referral assignments for our cloud team?
- Any difference in lead time for SOC2 audit artifacts / data residency assurances between marketplace listing vs private deployment?

We want to avoid double-billing windows and make sure our finance team can map spend to the right cost center. Any brief summary we can share with procurement would help.

Appreciate your guidance — happy to hop on a call if easier.

Best,
Emily Santos
Director, Clinical Platforms
MediPath Health
[emily.santos@medipath.com]


On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 09:15 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Emily — thanks for the note and great to hear the demo resonated.
>
> I pulled together a short primer for procurement; see below summary and I attached a SKU matrix that maps marketplace SKUs to direct-invoice SKUs. If you want, I can convert the primer into a one-page for your PO team.
>
> Quick answers up front:
> - Marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP private offer): Seller of Record typically remains Redwood (or our marketplace partner) and invoices are billed via marketplace channel. Invoice cadence is defined by the private offer (monthly/quarterly). Private offers can take 5–10 business days to process after procurement acceptance
> - Direct Invoice (Redwood): Redwood issues invoices directly; billing cadence can be customized (monthly/quarterly) and we can map to your cost centers faster for internal chargeback.
> - Co-sell credits / cloud incentives: Marketplace purchases often have co-sell credits via the marketplace partner program, but the timing and assignment depend on the cloud partner’s ISV co-sell process. Direct purchases allow us to assign credits or rebates directly under a Redwood sales agreement — often simpler for applying revenue recognition rules.
> - SOC2 / data residency: Artifact access and evidence are the same for both paths; what differs is the contracting and who is party to the PO. For private on-prem or VPC deployments we add contractual language for data residency and addenda.
>
> Attached: redwood_marketplace_sku_matrix.xlsx (maps marketplace SKUs to direct invoice SKUs)
>
> Next best step: If procurement confirms preferred invoice owner (marketplace vs Redwood), we’ll route a tailored private offer or draft an MSA amendment.
>
> Cheers,
> Neha Kapoor
> Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
> [Attachment: redwood_marketplace_sku_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot procurement questions — marketplace vs direct invoice

Team — looped you in to align on recommended path for MediPath pilot. Key asks from the customer: Seller of Record, invoice cadence, co-sell credit assignment, SOC2/data residency clarifications.

My read: they prefer predictable chargeback and tight cost-center mapping (leaning toward Redwood invoice) but want to keep marketplace co-sell benefits if possible. Two options to propose:

1) Marketplace private offer (fast to approve via cloud listings), Redwood remains Seller of Record, customer purchases via AWS/GCP private offer — benefits: cloud co-sell pipeline, marketplace incentives; cons: procurement mapping sometimes slower, partner revenue recognition nuances.

2) Direct Redwood invoice under a short PO + MSA amendment — benefits: clean ledger mapping and flexible billing cadence; cons: misses out on some marketplace co-sell attribution unless we coordinate with partner GTM (takes ~2 weeks).

Ask: Laura, can Legal confirm if we can include a clause to reserve co-sell attribution post-signature if they later move to marketplace? Vivek/Ben, please flag any finance implications (revenue split timelines, invoice maturity).

Thanks — I’ll draft a short note for the customer once we have internal alignment.

— Neha

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot procurement questions — marketplace vs direct invoice

Neha — legal ok on a clause to preserve co-sell attribution but we need to be explicit:

- Clause should state that if the customer moves to a marketplace private offer within X days of initial purchase (suggest 90 days), Redwood will work with the cloud partner to backdate co-sell attribution to the pilot start date, subject to partner approval.
- We should not guarantee partner acceptance; language should be "best efforts" and require customer cooperation to submit required contacts and evidence.

I'll draft suggested language and loop in our partner GTM contact to prep the cloud partner request. Also confirm: no SOC2 evidence gating difference between purchase paths — both get the same artifact access under our SOC2 attestation addendum.

— Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pilot procurement questions — marketplace vs direct invoice

Hi Jason / Emily — thanks for the checklist, that helped. Quick answers and proposed path so your AP can move forward without delay: 

Short answers:
- Credits/adjustments: If you start with a direct Redwood invoice and later transition to a marketplace private offer, we can coordinate with the cloud partner to request retroactive co-sell attribution. Practically, this is a partner-side approval and may not change prior invoices — any billing credit would be handled case-by-case but is uncommon. We typically preserve customer billing continuity and coordinate partner incentives outside of invoice rebilling.
- Seller of Record: For marketplace private offers the Seller of Record is often the partner (e.g., AWS Marketplace listing may show "Redwood" as the Seller, but in some resold arrangements the reseller appears). We will confirm the exact SOR string for Medipath when we create the private offer.

Recommended path for a low-friction pilot:
1) Proceed with a 3-month pilot under a Redwood direct invoice (monthly) for immediate procurement cadence and cost-center mapping. We’ll deliver an MSA amendment that includes a 90-day conversion window and a "co-sell preservation" clause (Laura to draft).
2) Parallel: Redwood will open the private-offer (marketplace) onboarding with our partner GTM to request attribution so that if Medipath elects to move to marketplace during the pilot we have the partner request already queued. This reduces rework and preserves co-sell eligibility.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (contains pilot scope, KPIs, and escalation contacts)

Next steps for MediPath AP:
- Sign MSA amendment + PO to Redwood (procurement center: AP code listed in your checklist).
- We’ll provide a one-page summary for your AP that maps invoice fields to their required fields.

If you want, we can also get our partner GTM on the same call next week to confirm SOR language for the private offer. Suggest a 30-minute slot Tuesday morning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
